about.title: About Consolidation Loan Calculator - Multi-Debt Consolidation Tool
about.description: The Consolidation Loan Calculator helps you evaluate whether combining multiple debts into a single loan changes monthly payments, total cost, and repayment timeline. It compares current debt payments with consolidation-loan scenarios so you can review tradeoffs across rates, fees, and terms. Use it as a planning reference when comparing consolidation options.

faq.q: When does debt consolidation make sense?
faq.a: Debt consolidation makes sense when you can secure a lower interest rate than your current average rate, simplify multiple payments, or need lower monthly payments. It's most beneficial for high-interest credit card debt consolidated into lower-rate loans.

faq.q: What types of loans can be used for debt consolidation?
faq.a: Common consolidation options include personal loans (6-36% APR), balance transfer credit cards (0-25% APR), home equity loans (5-10% APR), and 401k loans. Each has different qualification requirements, rates, and terms.

faq.q: Will debt consolidation hurt my credit score?
faq.a: Initially, debt consolidation may temporarily lower your credit score due to hard inquiries and new accounts. However, it can improve your score long-term by reducing credit utilization and establishing a consistent payment history.

faq.q: What are the risks of debt consolidation?
faq.a: Risks include potentially paying more interest over time if you extend repayment periods, accumulating new debt on cleared accounts, and possible fees. Some people lose motivation to pay off debt quickly with lower monthly payments.
